phys_3_1 G1.issue: Carbon-14 cannot date Olorgesailie (about a million years old, far beyond the 50,000-year limit); the supporting phenomenon and the Lesson 4 problem now use a Later Stone Age site, Lukenya Hill Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5730 years, so it can only date material younger than about 50,000 years (about 9 half-lives). Olorgesailie is roughly a million years old and is dated with potassium-argon / argon-argon methods, so using it for a carbon-14 problem is wrong. Lukenya Hill (Machakos County) is a Later Stone Age site with radiocarbon dates in the right range, so the story and the arithmetic (one-eighth left = 3 half-lives = 17 190 years) still work. Checked: 3 x 5730 = 17 190, well inside the 50,000-year limit. Teacher to confirm that Lukenya Hill (or another local radiocarbon-dated site, e.g. Hyrax Hill) is the site they prefer. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL Archaeologists at Later Stone Age sites like Lukenya Hill (Machakos County) use carbon-14 dating to determine the age of charcoal, bone and shell up to about 50,000 years old (much older sites such as Olorgesailie, about a million years old, are dated by other methods).
